subject: SIG/CAIQ sampling — proposed dry-run & control intake sequencing
messages:
From: Mike Locke <mike.locke@acmecorp.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example.com
Cc: security-team@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ intake & sample window — what we need next

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Acme's procurement team and InfoSec want to agree on a practical sampling plan for SIG/CAIQ and a short dry-run before the formal intake so our auditors have an exemplar. Two asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood provide a prioritized list of controls you expect to sample (CSV acceptable) and any preferred extraction windows for artifacts/logging?
2) Can we run a 2–3 day dry-run the week of May 15 to validate evidence retrieval and ACL access scopes?

We'd also like a short runbook that describes the handoff process so our auditor can find artifacts without chasing owners. If you have a template, please send it.

Thanks — Mike
Mike Locke
Sr. Security Manager, Acme Corp
From: alex_martinez@redwood.example.com
To: Mike Locke <mike.locke@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, irene_choi@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ intake & sample window — what we need next

Mike — appreciate the clear asks. Draft plan below and attached two artifacts: (1) a proposed sample set (sig-sample-proposal-20280505.csv) and (2) our intake template (acme-sig-caiq-intake-template.xlsx). High level approach: 

- Sample selection: we recommend a stratified sample across identity, configuration, and logging controls (20 items total: 12 high-priority, 6 medium, 2 low). CSV lists control IDs + owner + suggested artifact types.
- Window for artifacts: for logs/snapshots we prefer a 14-day window for any extraction we need; for config screenshots or policy docs a current export is sufficient.
- Dry-run scope: 48–72 hours to validate credentialed access, extraction commands, and an auditor view. We can do a targeted dry-run for 5–7 controls that represent each category.

Proposed timeline:
- May 10: intake kickoff + confirm owners and temporary access (you and procurement)
- May 15–17: dry-run (48–72h)
- May 20: reconcile gaps and finalize schedule for full sampling

Operational notes: please ensure a single point of contact on your side for access escalation during the dry-run. We'll provide a short runbook (see link in reply) and a pinned Slack channel for realtime coordination.

Attachment stubs: acme-sig-caiq-intake-template.xlsx (xlsx), sig-sample-proposal-20280505.csv (csv)

— Alex Martinez
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational clarifications from our side (I've been running point on auditor logistics for similar customers):

- Control owners: we'll need owners to acknowledge evidence transfer and the expected retention level (snapshot vs continuous export). Please confirm owner emails in the intake template.
- Retention & redaction: for any PII in logs we'll provide redacted extracts; if an unredacted artifact is required we'll require a secure transfer (SFTP with one-time creds).
- Dry-run acceptance criteria: success = auditor can locate the artifact and validate the control narrative with no more than two follow-ups. Failures will be triaged in a 1-hr warroom.

Irene — can you confirm the log extraction commands and whether we need an availability window longer than 14 days for retention sampling?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, alex_martinez@redwood.example.com, Mike Locke <mike.locke@acmecorp.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 05 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ intake & sample window — what we need next

Hi all — quick technical confirmation:

- Log extraction: we have a scripted export that pulls indexed event logs (kinesis -> s3 archive) by date range. For the dry-run we'll enable a scoped IAM role with read-only access to the relevant S3 prefixes; extraction command examples are in the attached intake template.
- Window: 14 days is fine for most controls. For retention sampling (e.g., log-archival verification) we'll need a bi-weekly snapshot for the last 90 days; if your audit requires longer, let us know and we'll schedule a separate extraction cadence.
- Artifacts and chain-of-custody: for any artifact we're generating a manifest file (sha256) and we can provide time-stamped exports to meet auditor traceability requirements.

Mike — if May 15 still works, we will:
1) send the intake template back with owner assignments by next Tue (May 9)
2) create the scoped role and S3 prefixes on May 12
3) run the dry-run May 15–17 and join a 30-min postmortem on May 18 to go over findings.

Attachment: acme-sig-caiq-intake-template.xlsx (contains extraction commands and manifest examples)

— Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
